That by which a mortal perceives, both in dream and in waking, by knowing that great all-pervading Atman the wise man grieves no more.

In these verses the teacher tries to make plain that all knowledge, as well as all sense perception, in every state of consciousnessâsleeping, dreaming or wakingâis possible only because the Self exists. There can be no knowledge or perception independent of the Self. Wise men, aware of this, identify themselves with their Higher Self and thus transcend the realm of grief.
citation: Anonymous; traditional Upanishadic corpus. The Upanishads. trans. Swami Paramananda. 1919
